result:
You've got it. Since you've handed me the how, I'll go with my pick below unless you object, and write the design up in my next message.

There are three realistic ways to build this:

1. **Add it to the taproom app you already run (my pick).** Batches, sack lots and bottling runs become new pages and tables in the same Flask app and SQLite database on the office Pi. A USB barcode scanner acts like a keyboard, so scanning a sack fills in the lot field on whatever screen the brewer has open. Labels print from the same Pi.
   - Trade-off: the tab system and batch tracking share one machine and one database. If the Pi goes down, both go down.
   - Why I'd pick it: it's one thing to run, back up and fix, and it uses what's already working.

2. **A separate small app beside it on the same Pi.** It would have its own database, so a problem in batch tracking can't touch the tabs.
   - Trade-off: two apps to update and two databases to back up. That's more upkeep for not much gain at your size.

3. **Off-the-shelf brewery software or a shared spreadsheet.** This means less to build.
   - Trade-off: it probably won't fit the scan-when-opened habit or your label printer. Your traceability records would also live somewhere else, and that's the thing you most need to trust.

This is big enough to need a proper written design rather than a few lines in chat. Before I hand it to you, a reviewer will read it as if they had to build from it, and I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer. This folder isn't under version control, so I'll save the design to `specs/batch-tracking.md`. Tell me if you'd rather I set up git so it's committed.
